source.title: Safeguarding LLM Fine-tuning via Push-Pull Distributional Alignment
source.authors: Haozhong Wang; Zhuo Li; Yi-Bo Yang; He Zhao; Hong-Yuan Zha; Dan-Dan Guo

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates harmfulness after fine-tuning on datasets that include harmful samples, using its own models, data, and evaluation setup rather than replicating the original protocol.
record.gate_note: The study reports harmfulness scores after standard SFT on mixed safe/harmful datasets, which bears on V1. It does not report an aligned, unfine-tuned model's harmfulness score for comparison. The harmful-ratio sweep reports Average Score rather than harmfulness separately. The cited claims in the introduction are not treated as this study's results.
record.test_reason: This is a defense paper proposing SOT, an optimal-transport data-weighting method. Harmful fine-tuning (10% HH red-team samples mixed into task data) serves as the attack setting. Standard SFT harmfulness is reported only as a baseline to beat. No HmS is given for the aligned models before fine-tuning, and there is no benign-only versus aligned-model comparison. The study therefore does not establish that fine-tuning raised harmful compliance. The harmful-ratio sweep (Fig. 2 middle) reports only the combined Average Score.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that SOT's dual-reference push-pull OT weighting and Top-K selection give the lowest harmfulness and the best safety-utility trade-off against all baselines, across four models and five datasets.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SFT on mixed downstream datasets with harmful samples, LoRA, and an LLM-judged red-team harmfulness measure; it does not reproduce the original fine-tuning protocol.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports outcome changes across harmful-data ratios, selection rates, reference-set sizes, the push-pull trade-off parameter, representation layers, and reference-data sources. The harmful-ratio sweep reports Average Score rather than harmfulness separately.
record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: No harmfulness result is reported for the aligned, unfine-tuned model, so the post-fine-tuning scores do not establish how much harmful compliance changed. Harmfulness is evaluated with an LLM judge, and the paper reports no uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 results are omitted because the flattened text does not reliably preserve the mapping of all values to models and datasets. The harmful-ratio sweep in Figure 2 is also omitted because it reports Average Score, not harmfulness separately.

untested.parts: Harmful compliance before versus after fine-tuning. Harmfulness as a function of the number or ratio of harmful examples (the sweep reports only Avg).
Benign-only fine-tuning harmfulness against the aligned model. The p=0 point in Fig. 2 is reported only as Avg.

missing.what: Standard SFT HmS for Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen3-8B on four datasets. For example, Llama-3.1 SLIMORCA HmS is 0.426, confirmed in Table 3. Like the other rows, these have no pre-fine-tuning baseline.

Text states that standard SFT and SEAL suffer precipitous degradation as harmful ratio p rises from 0 to 20%. This is the only dose-response evidence, and it is reported in Average Score, not harmfulness.

Top-K Only filtering lowers HmS to 0.205 versus Standard SFT at 0.426 (Llama-3.1, SLIMORCA). This indirectly implicates the harmful samples, but it is a method comparison, not a test against the aligned model.

record.verdict_notes: The paper takes fine-tuning-induced safety erosion as given, citing Qi et al. 2024b among others, and only measures defenses. Gemma-3-4b-it shows HmS of about 0.68 after standard SFT with 10% harmful data, which is suggestive of V1. Still, there is no aligned-model baseline, and HmS uses a DeepSeek-V3 yes/no judge with no uncertainty reported. For these reasons no verdict on V1 is given. If the aligned baseline is later sourced elsewhere, the rows could be reconsidered.

versions.untested_parts: No comparison with the same safety-aligned models before fine-tuning; the separately reported harmful-ratio sweep does not provide harmfulness scores by ratio.
No harmfulness result for benign-only fine-tuning compared with the aligned, unfine-tuned model.
No compliant-prefix, suffix, or decoding intervention.
No test of whether a small set of model weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
No test of whether data or training objectives cause safety to be shallow.
No training designed to deepen safety across response tokens.
